patch_description:
Builds on the two prior 1-parameter-per-block designs (candidate "theta" with RX/RY/RZ pre/post layers plus fixed CZ ring+diameter, and candidate "p_shared" with RY/RZ plus CZ ring+skip-2) that both reached score 0.80 but showed a trade-off: the RX+RY+CZ-ring+CZ-diameter+RZ variant converged much faster (60 steps) than the RY+CZ-ring+CZ-skip2+RZ variant (240 steps), while both had identical accuracy and parameter count (8 total, 1 unique per block).

The key insight is that the faster-converging variant used *two* non-commuting single-qubit rotation axes (RX then RY) before entangling, giving richer single-qubit expressivity per shared scalar, and used a *fixed* long-range entangler (diameter CZ). This version keeps that faster-converging single-qubit structure (RX, RY pre-layer; RZ post-layer, all reusing the same scalar "theta") but replaces one of the fixed long-range CZ diameter gates with a *parametrized* CRZ entangler on antipodal pairs that reuses the SAME shared scalar "theta" as the rotation gates (per the recommendation). This turns the previously "free" long-range entangling structure into a genuinely trainable, non-commuting two-qubit interaction, without adding a single extra trainable parameter (n_params stays fixed by the outer repetition count), potentially increasing the expressive power of the shared scalar and improving loss/generalization while preserving the fast-converging single-qubit backbone.

Gate budget is kept close to the best-performing prior variant (ring CZ for local connectivity + antipodal CRZ instead of antipodal CZ) to avoid unnecessary depth growth.
